attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'any', 'massively subsidized', 'can and will' and the stated cause. The sentence mixes a present subsidy claim with an undated forecast of degradation. The contract handles both parts, and the 'will' part is firm.

contract.note: A plain reading of the universal 'any' is fair and ordinary. Separating API retail value from provider cost is reasonable. No deadline is given, so it can resolve early only on evidence covering the whole scope or on a definitive counterexample.

evidence.note: Anthropic moved third-party tool use onto extra usage on April 4 and cited capacity. This is before the post and covers one provider, so it cannot fulfil a forward-looking universal claim.

Modelled break-even utilization based on SemiAnalysis, comparing price with API-equivalent value. It depends on assumptions, covers two providers, and does not show provider cost for every subscription.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated and no conclusive event covers the whole scope. The packet has no product-level cost accounts showing that every subscription is massively subsidized. It also has no dated record of degradation across all products after the post. The one-provider restriction comes before the post, and the economics are modelled estimates.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'incredibly demanding' framing, the listed setup burdens, and the aside that agents will cause problems. In context the claim is mainly about the multi-agent setups AI boosters describe.

contract.note: Reading it as substantial required setup and supervision is fair. The Jan–Mar 2026 window and the line drawn between developer work and end-user work are the evaluator's choices. The speaker set no threshold for 'demanding'.

evidence.note: Dated Feb 2026 research write-up showing heavy harness work and agents overwriting each other's changes. It is one demanding research prototype, not a representative sample of products.

First-hand Jan 2026 look at Cowork, a packaged agent that starts from a single prompt. It weakly counters 'must set it up' for packaged products, but it is single-agent and does not measure supervision.

reviews.rationale: The contract asks for representative evidence. The packet has one research prototype showing heavy setup and coordination failures, and one packaged single-agent demo showing little setup. Neither measures typical user burden or how often coordination failures happen across agentic workflows in the period, so the outcome is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I believe things will only get worse' states a firm expectation, not a graded hedge. The antecedent 'as capacity issues continue' is kept. The 'insane and deceptive' part is opinion and is rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'things' as customer access, allowances, prices and reliability at OpenAI and Anthropic fits the context. Requiring that constraints continue at the time of any improvement keeps the conditional intact.

evidence.note: Secondary report from April 22 describing an ongoing capacity crunch after the post. It supports the antecedent, not the outcome.

Anthropic's own disclosure that it doubled Claude Code limits and removed peak-hour cuts on May 6. It credits new compute, so it is unclear the capacity condition still held. That means it does not meet the contradiction rule.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The May 6 improvement is real, but Anthropic links it to capacity being relieved. So the packet does not show that constraints were continuing when it happened, and the early-resolution rule is not met. A limited period of worsening also cannot prove 'only get worse' without a horizon.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Captures the core claims: the services are unprofitable and unsustainable, and more capacity means bigger losses. It leaves out the 'must' framing about burning less money and rationing capacity, which is secondary.

contract.note: The speaker named no accounting basis or period. Calendar 2025 and the need for separate, service-level and marginal evidence are evaluator choices. They are reasonable because the key element is causal.

evidence.note: Audited S-1, available Oct 26, showing Anthropic's GAAP net losses for 2025, mostly from fair-value changes. Company-wide losses say nothing about what extra capacity does at the margin.
Press estimate that OpenAI's 2025 adjusted gross margin was a positive 33%. It cuts against service-level losses but does not measure what an extra capacity purchase contributes.
Epoch's estimate of Anthropic's 2025 EBITDA loss, based on press-reported projections. It is consistent with losses but does not establish the causal claim.
Epoch reports an estimated 40% gross margin for Anthropic in 2025. An average margin does not settle what extra capacity does at the margin.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows company-level losses at Anthropic and estimated positive gross margins at both firms. Nothing in it measures whether buying more capacity raises losses once the revenue it enables is counted. The core causal claim is therefore unsettled, and the accounting bases do not match.
